page: Microsoft Azure FX8-4mds_v2 is a memory-intensive virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor with a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The configuration includes 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 168.0 GB of system memory, yielding 42.0 GB of RAM per core, alongside a 472 GB local NVMe SSD. No GPUs are included, and it offers zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-core capabilities, with Geekbench single-core and text processing scores reaching top-tier classifications. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also demonstrate strong performance. However, multi-core and large-block memory bandwidth benchmarks show relative weaknesses. The stress-ng multi-core CPU test and large-block uncached memory read/write bandwidth tests fall into the weak category. Database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput perform at average levels.

The hardware profile offers high memory density relative to the low vCPU count, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel processing. The primary trade-off is the contrast between excellent single-core execution and weaker multi-threaded scaling. This server is suited for memory-intensive database operations, in-memory caching, text processing, and lightweight single-threaded data manipulation.
